 
 Keep keys out of task comments and bot memory · Spec 
 Keep keys out of task comments and bot memory · Spec v2 · 2026-11-17
 Cause: A key pasted into a task comment is stored and shown to every reader and bot: the key detector guards only the Tools chat. The turn scrub also misses keys written as JSON escapes or UTF-16.
 Fix: Check every task text field with the detector's rules; teach the scrub the encoded forms.
 Decide: OK this spec, or send it back. Two choices at OK are yours (Open questions).
 Before and after
 Today POST /api/v2/tasks/{id}/comments
text: "deploy key: <a GitHub token>"
→ 200, stored as typed; every reader and
 bot on the task sees it.
A turn writes a granted key into memory/,
with JSON escapes or in a UTF-16 file
→ committed and pushed as is.
 After the fix Same comment
→ 422, a key was found, save it in Tools.
 Nothing stored; an audit row, no value.
Same turn
→ escaped form masked before the commit;
 UTF-16 file left out and named in the reply.
 No screen changes but the refusal's words (UX Writer's).
 Details
 Goal
 Who has it: every company, every task. No incident known; evidence from code.
 How we will know: keys kept out of comments per week, from audit rows that hold no value. Baseline: none, no check today (2026-11-17). Target: missing, yours to set; proposed: every certain-tier key kept out. Guard: wrongful refusals from support requests, baseline 0; narrow the rules if more than 2 accounts report one. Read 14 days after release.
 Appetite: small batch, up to 2 engineer-weeks, one engineer (Security Owner, 2026-11-17). If declined: logged with a date to look again.
 Step 1: the check (code read, acme/tico at ef180c3a9)
 Store Today Gap 
 Task comments and bodies No key check; the detector ( secret_drop.py ) runs only in the Tools chat. Open: a pasted key is stored and shown. 
 Bot memory, pushed files Changed files scrubbed of granted secrets (plain, URL, base64); binary ones left out ( redact.rs ). JSON escapes, UTF-16 missed; ungranted keys unknown. 
 Logs, run events Scrubbed of granted values ( scrub_log ). Same encoded forms. Server logs not read (open question). 
 Browser action log Verb and page path only. None found; a test keeps it so. 
 Scope and non-goals
 In: every task text write checked with the certain-tier rules before storing, from any client, person or bot: comments and their edits, title, body, note (done, update), ask text, answer values, public title and summary (criteria 1 to 7).
 In: the turn scrub (Rust and Python alike) matches granted secrets JSON-escaped and in UTF-16 LE/BE, in files, logs and events.
 In: one shared test set of gstack's cases (A to E below), run by both runners.
 Droppable: the same rules over changed memory/ files.
 Out: keys already stored; suspect-tier matches; channel messages (next brief); meeting transcripts; a value split inside itself; rotating keys.
 Acceptance criteria
 Given a person, when they post a comment holding a certain-tier key from the web, then it is refused, nothing stored, and the message names Tools, not the key. before release 
 Given a bot, when it posts the same comment with tico task comment , then it is refused the same way. before release 
 Given any other task text write listed in scope, including one inside a hand-off (done with a note, an answer), when it holds a key, then it is refused the same way and the task is left unchanged at the same version. before release 
 Given a comment from Slack, mail or a public requester on a roadmap task holding a key, when it is stored, then the key reads as a mark and the author is told where it still is. before release 
 Given any refusal or mark in 1 to 4, when the audit is read, then one row names the task, author and rule, with no value, hash or partial characters. before release 
 Given a refusal to a bot, when it reads the answer, then it gets the stable code looks_like_key and one line it can act on: save it in Tools and refer to it by name. before release 
 Given text with no key (task UUIDs, file-ids, 40-hex git hashes, PR URLs, s3:// URIs, Tico-Run lines, addresses, prose about keys), when it is posted, then it is stored unchanged; the detector's negative cases and this page's text pass. before release 
 Case A. Given a granted secret, when a turn writes it JSON-escaped into a memory file, then it is masked before the commit. before release 
 Case B. Given a granted secret, when a turn writes a UTF-16 file holding it, then the file is left out of the commit and named in the reply. before release 
 Case C. Given a granted secret, when a turn writes token= and the value on the next line, in UTF-8 and UTF-16, then each is masked or left out as in 8 and 9. before release 
 Case D. Given a granted secret, when a turn writes a file git treats as binary holding it, then the file is left out, as today. before release 
 Case E. Given a memory file with an Authorization: line, when a turn changes only its value to a granted secret, then the new value is masked before the commit. before release 
 Given a granted key written with JSON escapes or in UTF-16 in a turn's log or events, when the log is read, then it shows as the mark. before release 
 Given a bot that types a secret into a website, when Activity is read, then it shows the verb and page path only. before release 
 Given 14 days in production, when the Support Owner's digests are read, then at most 2 accounts reported a wrongful refusal. Watched by Security Owner. after launch 
 v2 (2026-11-17): all task text paths, unchanged task on refusal, stable code, Tico id negatives, roadmap comments masked (Tasks Product Owner's input).
 Not proved yet: how often people paste keys into comments today.
 Open questions
 Refuse, or store masked, for comments typed in Tico? Default refuse, as in the Tools chat. Ana, you decide at OK.
 A one-off read-only count of existing comments holding a key (task ids only, no values)? Default no. Ana, at OK.
 Do server logs record request bodies? Engineering, by 2026-11-24.
 Risks: false refusals. Observed: run over a draft of this page, the certain-tier rules flagged three ordinary phrases as keys. Criterion 7 must pass before release. 
 Ben checks this page. Ana, you OK it.
